subject.title: [Feature]: Add global --dry-run mode to prevent all tool calls from executing

question: What request-scoped no-side-effects contract should OpenClaw expose for global agent tool dry-run across CLI, Gateway/embedded runs, built-in/plugin/client tools, direct tool invocation, Codex/native runtime hooks, and before/after hooks?
rationale: The request would create a security-relevant product guarantee, and current source shows several execution surfaces that a narrow process-global adapter flag would not safely cover.

options.title: Design request-scoped core dry-run
options.body: Specify the runtime contract first, then implement an additive CLI/runtime path with tests for built-in, plugin, client, Gateway, embedded, direct-invoke, and hook behavior.

options.title: Fold into workflow modes
options.body: Keep this issue open but block implementation until broader Ask/Plan/Modify or scoped-agent mode defines the shared preview vocabulary and guarantees.

options.title: Reject global dry-run
options.body: Leave scoped command-level dry-runs only if maintainers decide a global preview boundary is too easy to misunderstand as a full sandbox guarantee.

recommendation.title: Design request-scoped core dry-run
recommendation.body: Specify the runtime contract first, then implement an additive CLI/runtime path with tests for built-in, plugin, client, Gateway, embedded, direct-invoke, and hook behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This is product/security-contract shaped and this handle has the strongest history across the central tool adapter, CLI, and Gateway surfaces.
